ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Rachel Carson

code.originalText: Start of letrozole, ribociclib, and zoledronic acid after radiation

text.paragraph: Start of letrozole, ribociclib, and zoledronic acid after radiation. [S]

Ms. Carson completed whole-breast and regional nodal radiation with a tumor-bed boost two and a half weeks ago, in 19 afternoon sessions, with mild reddening of the skin that has faded. She kept writing in the mornings throughout. Her dental check last week was normal. Today she starts letrozole and the first 28-day cycle of ribociclib, and has her first zoledronic acid infusion. She has read the side-effect sheets and asked for the monitoring schedule in writing, which she was given. She has mild morning knee stiffness, unchanged, and no hot flashes. She takes no other medicines and no grapefruit or herbal products. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Left breast with faint tanning and mild firmness after radiation; scar healed; no masses. Right breast normal
Arm circumference 25.5 cm on each side; full shoulder movement; knees with mild crepitus, no effusion
Teeth and gums in good repair

Invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast, upper outer quadrant at 2 o'clock, 2.4 cm on imaging; core biopsy grade 2, estrogen and progesterone receptor positive, HER2 negative, Ki-67 22 percent; clinical stage T2 N0 (cT2 cN0 M0); synthetic modern counterpart of the documented 1960 breast cancer, which was not disclosed to her
S — Synthetic tumor details, stage, and treatment; the breast lumps, the 1960 operation, and the nondisclosure are documented (D), but no tumor details from her lifetime are used.
Estrogen receptor positive status of the breast cancer (ER 95 percent, PR 80 percent)
S — Synthetic receptor result; no receptor status from her lifetime is known.
New firm lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, found two weeks ago; clinically suspicious; diagnostic imaging and biopsy booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the biopsy diagnosis; the lumps in the left breast in early 1960 are documented (D).
Duodenal ulcer found at endoscopy seven weeks ago, with Helicobacter pylori on biopsy; treated with 14 days of bismuth quadruple therapy and completing eight weeks of omeprazole; test of cure planned
S — Synthetic modern ulcer; it echoes the ulcer among her documented illnesses, which the sources do not date.
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, mild, with stiffness after long walks on the shore
S — Synthetic condition; it is not linked to the documented word arthritis, which she may have used to keep her cancer private.
Metastatic carcinoma in two of three left axillary sentinel lymph nodes (macrometastases, no extranodal extension); pathologic stage pT2 pN1a(sn) M0, anatomic stage IIB; recurrence score 17
S — Synthetic surgical pathology; spread to lymph nodes is documented later in her life, but no pathology from her lifetime is used.
Long-term use of letrozole as adjuvant endocrine therapy, with ribociclib for three years
Low bone mass (osteopenia) on baseline DXA before letrozole: lumbar spine T-score -1.8, femoral neck -1.3; 10-year major osteoporotic fracture risk about 7 percent (FRAX); vitamin D insufficiency
S — Synthetic finding on the baseline DXA the protocol requires for an aromatase inhibitor.

list.item:
Letrozole with ribociclib, starting today (Z79.811). Baseline QTcF 418 ms, below the 450 ms limit for starting ribociclib. Neutrophils 3.4, liver tests normal, potassium 4.2, magnesium 2.1, calcium 9.4. No interacting drugs. [S]
Letrozole 2.5 mg daily.
Ribociclib 400 mg on days 1 to 21 of each 28-day cycle.
ECG at about day 14; blood count and liver tests every two weeks for two cycles, then at the start of the next four cycles; electrolytes at the start of each of the first six cycles.
Fever of 38.0 °C or more, palpitations, fainting, yellow eyes, or dark urine to be reported the same day.

Low bone mass on baseline DXA, with vitamin D insufficiency (M85.80). Lumbar spine T-score -1.8, femoral neck -1.3; 10-year major fracture risk about 7 percent. Letrozole speeds bone loss; the adjuvant zoledronic acid she chose also protects bone. Vitamin D 22 ng/mL, creatinine 0.8, eGFR 87, calcium normal. [S]
Zoledronic acid 4 mg intravenously today, then every six months for three years.
Vitamin D3 1000 units daily and calcium from food.
Weight-bearing and strength exercise.
Repeat DXA in two years.

Knee osteoarthritis (M17.0). Mild and stable; recorded as the baseline before letrozole, which can cause joint aches. [S]
Walking and quadriceps exercises; acetaminophen as needed.

list.item: Receive the biopsy result in person within ten days, explained in plain words, with a copy of the report. Outcome by 2026-03-18: Told the diagnosis in person nine days after presentation, with the pathology report in hand; teach-back confirmed her understanding [S]

Make each treatment decision herself after hearing the options, benefits, and harms. Outcome by 2026-04-20: Chose breast-conserving surgery and, after the pathology, radiation, letrozole, ribociclib, and zoledronic acid [S]

Complete surgery and radiation, then start endocrine therapy, within four months of diagnosis. Outcome by 2026-06-15: Lumpectomy at three weeks, radiation completed at ten weeks, letrozole and ribociclib started at thirteen weeks [S]
Take adjuvant systemic therapy safely, with every safety check the drugs require done on schedule. In progress; target 2026-12-07 [S]
Keep writing at least four mornings a week through treatment. In progress; target 2026-12-07 [S]
